note: The viewfinder's numbers (commons/void/camcorder_hud.gd reads them; commons/void/hud_config.gd carries them). A file of this shape sent to a running game with `python tools/push_hud_config.py <file>` (or single values with --set) is laid over this one and takes effect within half a second, no build. Only the keys you want to change need be sent. vr: the plane in a headset. frame_width_m and frame_height_m are its size, distance_m how far in front of the eyes it floats (its edge is atan(frame_width_m / 2 / distance_m) degrees out to the side: 1.66 at 1.2 = 35), vertical_offset_m moves the whole plane down (negative) or up, pixels_wide is the sharpness of its picture. text_scale multiplies the letter size. elements places each item on the plane: `at` [x, y] as shares of the picture (0 0 top left, 1 1 bottom right; y is the middle of the item's row), `align` left / center / right (which edge of the item sits at x), `show`, and for the two texts `width` (the share of the picture's width they may take; the map's name is cut with an ellipsis, the sung line wraps upward). Palle 2026-11-16: in a headset everything in one row at the bottom, nearer the middle: the map's name left, the charge right, the sung line between; the REC plate and the corner marks are off there. desktop: no elements, so the overlay keeps its corners; margin_scale, sung_line_at (0 = just above the bottom row) and sung_line_width are for that layout.
